t.3.71.1: When Śabarī had gone to heaven by virtue of her own deeds, Rāghava, together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, began to reflect.
t.3.71.2: Having reflected on that power of the great-souled ones, the righteous Rāghava spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, who was devoted to his welfare and wholly attentive.
t.3.71.3: Gentle one, we have seen this hermitage of those whose selves are perfected. It is full of many wonders, its deer and tigers live free of fear, and birds of many kinds frequent it.
t.3.71.4: O Lakṣmaṇa, in these sacred fords of the seven oceans the ritual ablution has been duly performed, and the ancestors too have been satisfied with offerings.
t.3.71.5: That inauspiciousness has vanished and good fortune has arrived; for that reason, Lakṣmaṇa, this mind of mine is now filled with joy.
t.3.71.6: Indeed, O tiger among men, something auspicious will arise in your heart. So come, we two shall go to that Pampā, lovely to behold.
t.3.71.7: There, not far off, shines Mount Ṛśyamūka, on which dwells the righteous-souled Sugrīva, son of the Sun, ever terrified out of fear of Vālin, together with four monkeys.
t.3.71.8: I am eager to see that Sugrīva, the bull among monkeys, for my search for Sītā depends on him, O gentle one.
t.3.71.9: To Rāma, who was speaking thus, Saumitri said this: "Let us two go there quickly; my mind too is hastening."
t.3.71.10: Then, having gone out from that hermitage, that lord of the people, the mighty one, came thereafter to Pampā together with Lakṣmaṇa.
t.3.71.12: That Rāma, tormented by longing, gazing upon trees of many kinds and lakes of many kinds, went on to a supreme lake.
t.3.71.11: As he gazed on every side at the forest rich in flowers and full of mighty trees, that great forest resounded with koyaṣṭis and arjunakas, with śatapattras and kīcakas, and with these and many other kinds of birds.
t.3.71.13: Having come from afar to that water-bearing stream, Rāma plunged into the lake called Mataṃgasarasa.
t.3.71.14: But Rāma, son of Daśaratha, overcome with grief, entered Pampā, the lotus lake, covered all over with lotuses.
t.3.71.16: rich in waters like crystal, spread with smooth sand, crowded with fish and tortoises, and adorned with trees standing upon its banks.
t.3.71.15: That lake is filled with tilaka, aśoka, puṃnāga, bakula and uddālaka trees, crowded with lovely groves, its waters thickly pressed with lotuses.
t.3.71.17: She is entwined by creepers as if by devoted female companions, frequented by Kiṃnaras, Uragas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, and strewn with many kinds of trees and creepers: a lovely, auspicious treasury of cool water.
t.3.71.18: Copper-red with lotuses and saugandhika blossoms, white with clusters of kumuda lilies, and blue with masses of blue water-lilies, she is many-hued like a variegated rug.
t.3.71.20: Then, having seen that Pampā, the radiant Rāma, son of Daśaratha, together with Saumitri, lamented out of longing.
t.3.71.19: That lake, rich in day-lotuses and blue water lilies, filled with padma and fragrant saugandhika blossoms, bordered by groves of flowering mango trees, and resounding with the loud cries of peacocks.
t.3.71.21: With tilaka trees and citrons, with banyans and śukladruma trees as well, with blossoming karavīras and with puṃnāgas in full flower.
t.3.71.23: On the bank of this lake stands the mountain I spoke of before, adorned with minerals and known as Ṛśyamūka, its woods bright with many-colored blossoms.
t.3.71.22: She is adorned like a lovely young woman with thickets of mālatī and kunda, with bhaṇḍīra and nicula trees, with aśokas, saptaparṇas, ketakas and atimuktakas, and with many other kinds of trees.
t.3.71.24: The monkey Sugrīva, son of that great-souled one named Ṛkṣarajas, a hero of great valour and widely renowned, dwells upon that mountain.
t.3.71.26: Then, having gradually travelled the great road, a path whose crossing was long, and gazing about at the forest, he beheld Pampā, its woods lovely to behold, thronged with many birds of every kind.
t.3.71.25: "Go to Sugrīva, the lord of the monkeys, O bull among men." Thus he spoke these words once more to Lakṣmaṇa of true valour.
